args.title: checkout-api health check failures after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary:
checkout-api began failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) following the deploy of v2.3.1. Observed error rate was 18% with the service reporting unhealthy.

Action taken: Rolled back checkout-api in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production (per release history: v2.2.9 healthy, v2.3.0 healthy, v2.3.1 unhealthy; v2.3.1-rc was a staging build and unhealthy, so it was not a rollback candidate).

The first rollback attempt failed partway with an orchestrator error, halting after us-east (leaving us-east on v2.3.0 while us-west and eu-west remained on v2.3.1). A retry of the rollback completed successfully across all three regions.

Current state: All regions on v2.3.0, service reports healthy, error rate down to ~0.2%.

Follow-up needed: Root-cause analysis on what changed in v2.3.1 that caused health check failures before any re-deploy attempt.

trace.final:
The incident was created successfully (the timeout was on the response, not the action) — so I did not retry, avoiding a duplicate page.

## Summary

**Rolled back checkout-api to v2.3.0 in all production regions and opened INC-0001 (SEV2).**

**What I found:**
- checkout-api was on **v2.3.1** in us-east, us-west, and eu-west — unhealthy, 18% error rate.
- Release history showed v2.2.9 (healthy), v2.3.0 (healthy), v2.3.1 (unhealthy), plus a v2.3.1-rc staging build that was also unhealthy. Since the target must be healthy **in production**, **v2.3.0** was the correct rollback target — v2.3.1-rc was disqualified on both environment and health.

**Rollback:** The first attempt failed partway with an orchestrator error, halting after us-east — leaving a split state (us-east on v2.3.0, us-west and eu-west still on the failing v2.3.1). I verified that state rather than assuming success, then retried, which completed cleanly across all three regions. No change-manager approval was needed, as v2.3.0 has previously been healthy in production.

**Verified end state:** All three regions on v2.3.0, `healthy: true`, error rate down from 18% → 0.2%.

**Incident:** INC-0001, SEV2, open with full description of the failure, the rollback (including the partial-failure retry), and the current healthy state.

**Two things worth flagging:**
1. **Root cause is unknown.** v2.3.1 was rolled back, not fixed. It shouldn't be re-deployed until whatever broke health checks is identified — I noted this in the incident as the follow-up action.
2. **The deploy pipeline may have a reliability issue.** The orchestrator error mid-rollout left production in a mixed-version state, which is worth a separate look — a rollback that half-succeeds during an active incident is a risky failure mode.
